(Benefit)
He said to His Prophet: ﴿Say: I am not a novelty among the messengers, and I do not know what will be done with me or with you﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 9].
And He said to His Prophet: ﴿And never say of anything, "Indeed, I will do that tomorrow," (23) unless [you add], "If Allah wills"﴾.
Then He sent down to His Prophet that his past and future sins had been forgiven. He means, and Allah knows best, that his past sins before the revelation and his future sins before He protected him so that he would not sin. (Subtlety)
How great is the difference between the Messenger of Allah ﷺ being expelled from Makkah in that state, and his entry into it in that manner, which no human being has ever rejoiced in as he did for the sake of Allah. He was surrounded from before him, behind him, on his right and on his left by the Muhajirun and the Ansar, who encircled him, with the angels above them, and the revelation from Allah descending upon him. He had entered His sanctuary in that manner. So where is the harm in that expulsion, which was as if it had never been?!

(Benefit)
His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, We have granted you a clear victory﴾.
This is the victory that Allah granted him, and Allah rewarded him for it with four things:
The forgiveness of his past and future sins.
The completion of His blessing upon him.
His guidance to a straight path.
The victorious support of Allah for him, a mighty victory.
With this, the answer is given to the question that some have raised here, saying: How can Allah's decree concerning him be the cause of these four matters, since Allah, Exalted is He, says: ﴿Indeed, We have granted you a clear victory, that Allah may forgive you your past and future sins﴾?
The answer is what we have mentioned: his acceptance of this decree, his contentment with it, his submission to it, and his entering under it, obliged Allah to give him that.

(Issue)
If it is asked: Why does the word [al-Sirat] (the path) come indefinite in His saying to His Prophet ﷺ: ﴿and guide you to a straight path﴾,
and His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And indeed, you guide to a straight path﴾, and His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And We chose them and guided them to a straight path﴾,
and His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Say: My Lord has guided me to a straight path﴾?
The answer to these instances is one answer: they are not in the context of supplication and request, but in the context of information from Allah, Exalted is He, about His guidance to a straight path and the guidance of His Messenger to it. The addressees had no prior acquaintance with it, and it was not known to them. Therefore it did not come definite with the definite article of prior reference, which points to something known in the mind of the addressee and present in his thoughts, nor was there any previously mentioned referent in the wording that would make the article known to him.
The definite article of prior reference comes in one of two cases: when there is a mentally known referent or a previous verbal mention. Since neither exists in these instances, indefiniteness is the basic form.
This is unlike His saying: ﴿Guide us to the straight path﴾. Since it was established among the addressees that Allah has a straight path to which He guided His prophets and messengers, and since the one addressed in the supplication, Glorified is He, knew it, the article was attached to it, and so He said: ﴿Guide us to the straight path﴾.
Al-Suhayli said: His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And guide you to a straight path﴾ was revealed concerning the treaty of al-Hudaybiyyah, when the Muslims disliked that treaty and considered that the right course was otherwise. Allah is exalted above what they say, and His Messenger ﷺ knew better. So Allah sent down this verse to His Messenger ﷺ. Thus it does not mean a straight path in religion, but a path in judgment, war and strategy.
As for His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And indeed, you guide to a straight path﴾,
that is, you guide from disbelief and misguidance to a straight path.
If He had said in this context "to the straight path," it would have given disbelief and misguidance a share of uprightness, since the definite article indicates that what it is attached to is more entitled to that meaning than what follows it in mention, or what is closer to it in the mind, and it is not entitled to it unless there is some part of it in the latter.
It is not hidden how weak and feeble these two answers are.
As for his claim that what is meant by His saying: ﴿and guide you to a straight path﴾ is in war and strategy, this diminishes this great favour and abundant portion with which Allah bestowed grace upon the Messenger ﷺ. The Prophet ﷺ informed that this verse was dearer to him than the world and all that is in it. When did Allah ever name war and strategy a straight path?
Has anyone, from the predecessors or the later scholars, interpreted this verse in that way? Rather, the straight path is what Allah placed upon it of guidance and the religion of truth, which He commanded him to report that Allah had guided him to, in His saying: ﴿Say: My Lord has guided me to a straight path﴾. Then He explained it with His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿a correct religion, the creed of Abraham, a man of pure faith, and he was not of those who associate others with Allah﴾. The word (religion) here is in the accusative as a substitute for the prepositional phrase, meaning: He guided me to a correct religion.

Reflect: what Allah, Glorified is He, gathered for His Messenger in the verse of victory from kinds of gifts. They are five things:
The first: the clear victory.
The second: the forgiveness of his past and future sins.
The third: His guidance to the straight path.
The fourth: the completion of His blessing upon him.
The fifth: the bestowal of mighty victory. Glorified is He gathered for him between guidance and victory, because by these two foundations complete happiness and success are achieved. Guidance is knowledge of Allah, Exalted is He, and His religion, and acting in pursuit of His pleasure and obedience to Him. It is beneficial knowledge and righteous action. Victory is complete power to implement His religion: by proof, clarity, the sword and the spear. Victory is by proof and clarity, and by subduing the hearts of those who oppose him through proof, and subduing their bodies by the hand. Glorified is He often combines these two foundations, for by them the call is completed and His religion is made to prevail over all religion, as in His saying: ﴿It is He who sent His Messenger with guidance and the religion of truth﴾, in two places in Surat Bara'ah and in Surat al-Saff.
And He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿We sent Our messengers with clear evidences, and sent down with them the Book and the balance, that people may establish justice﴾. This is guidance.
Then He said: ﴿And We sent down iron, wherein is great might﴾. This is victory. So He mentioned the Book, the guide, and the iron, the helper.
And He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿Alif, Lam, Mim. Allah, there is no deity except Him, the Ever-Living, the Sustainer. He has sent down upon you, [O Muhammad], the Book in truth, confirming what was before it. And He revealed the Torah and the Gospel before, as guidance for the people, and He revealed the criterion﴾.

The secret of linking victory with guidance is that each of them achieves the distinction between truth and falsehood. (Section)
The scholar Ibn al-Qayyim said, after mentioning the disagreement among people about the grateful rich and the patient poor, which of them is better:
If it is said: Which is better: one who chooses wealth to give charity and spend in the ways of righteousness, or one who chooses poverty and frugality to stay away from trial and be safe from calamity, and to ease his heart in preparation for the Hereafter, so that worldly matters do not occupy him, or one who chooses neither this nor that, but chooses what Allah has chosen for him, so that he does not specify by his own choice either of the two?
It is said: This is a matter in which the states of the pious predecessors differed. Some of them chose wealth to fight with it, to spend, and to disburse it in ways of righteousness, like Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf and other wealthy Companions.
Qays ibn Sa'd used to say: "O Allah, I am among Your servants who will not be set right except by wealth."
Others chose poverty and frugality, like Abu Dharr and a group of Companions with him.
These looked at the calamities of the world and feared trial by it.
Those looked at the benefits of spending and its fruits, both immediate and deferred.
The third group chose nothing; rather, their choice was what Allah chose for them.
Likewise with choosing a long life in the world to establish the religion of Allah and worship Him: one group chose it and wished for it, and another group loved death, meeting Allah, and rest from the world.
A third group chose neither this nor that, but chose what Allah chooses for them, and their choice was tied to what Allah wills, without a specific desire of their own.
This was the state of al-Siddiq, may Allah be pleased with him. When they said to him in his final illness: "Shall we not call a physician for you?" he said: "He has seen me." They said: "What did He say to you?" He said: "He said to me: 'Indeed, I do what I will.'"
The first was the state of Moses, peace be upon him. When the Angel of Death came to him, he slapped him and gouged out his eye. That was not out of love for the world and life in it, but in order to carry out his Lord's commands, establish His religion, and fight His enemies. It was as if he said to the Angel of Death: "You are a commanded servant, and I am a commanded servant, and I am in carrying out my Lord's commands and establishing His religion." When a long life was offered to him, and he knew that death would come after it, he chose what Allah had chosen for him.
As for our Prophet, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him, his Lord sent to him, informing him, and he was the most knowledgeable of creation about Allah. He knew that his Lord, blessed and exalted is He, loved to meet him and chose it for him. So he chose meeting Allah. Had he known that his Lord loved for him to remain in the world to carry out His commands and establish His religion, he would not have chosen otherwise. His choice followed the choice of his Lord, Mighty and Majestic is He. Just as when his Lord gave him the option between being a king-prophet and being a servant-prophet, and he knew his Lord chose for him to be a servant-prophet, he chose what Allah chose for him. Thus his choice in all his affairs followed Allah's choice for him. For this reason, on the day of al-Hudaybiyyah, he bore what he bore of that state at that time, fulfilled that station its due, and none remained steadfast with him in every respect except al-Siddiq. He had no choice in anything other than what Allah had chosen for him and for his Companions in that state in which the matter was settled. So he was content with it, choosing it, witnessing his Lord's choice of it. This is the utmost of servanthood. So Allah thanked him for that, and his thanks was what He gave him good news of at the beginning of Surat al-Fath, until the Companions congratulated him on it and said: "Congratulations to you, O Messenger of Allah." He had a right to be congratulated with the greatest thing with which any human has been congratulated, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him.

(Section)
Among what should be known is that every characteristic of excellence, Allah has placed His Messenger at its highest point and specially honoured him with its summit. So when a sect of the community that recognized these characteristics and divided them among themselves for their own excellence over others uses his state as evidence, the other sect may also use him as evidence for its own excellence. When the warriors and fighters use it to claim they are the best of groups, the scholars and jurists can use it in the same way that those did.
When ascetics and those who turned away from the world use it to claim their excellence, those who engage with the world, governance and ruling the subjects in order to establish the religion of Allah and carry out His command, can use it.
When the patient poor use it, the grateful rich can use it.
When the people of worship use it to prove the excellence and preference of voluntary worship, the knowers can use it to prove the excellence of knowledge.
When the people of humility and forbearance use it, the people of might and dominance can use it against falsehood, for severity toward them and striking them.
When the people of dignity, awe and gravity use it, the people of good character and permissible humour that does not depart from truth, and good companionship with family and friends, can use it.
When those who proclaim the truth and speak it openly, in public and in private, use it, the people of gentleness, modesty and generosity can use it to hasten to tell a man what he dislikes to his face.
When the scrupulous use it to support praiseworthy scrupulousness, the facilitators who do not depart from the breadth, ease and smoothness of His Law can use it.
When one who directs his concern to correcting his religion and heart uses it, one who attends to correcting his body, livelihood and worldly life can use it, for he was sent for the welfare of both the world and religion.
When one whose heart is not attached to means and does not rely on them uses it, one who engages with means and places them in their proper positions and gives them their due can use it.
When one who hungers and endures hunger uses it, one who is full and thanks his Lord for fullness can use it. When one who takes pardon, forgiveness and forbearance uses it, one who takes revenge in the places of revenge can use it.
When one who gives for Allah and befriends for Allah uses it, one who withholds for Allah and opposes for Allah can use it.
When one who does not store anything for tomorrow uses it, one who stores for his family the provision of a year can use it.
When one who eats coarse food and condiments, like barley bread and vinegar, uses it, one who eats delicious and good food, like roasted meat, sweets, fruit and melon and the like, can use it.
When one who fasts continuously uses it, one who breaks the fast continuously can use it, so that he would fast until it is said he never breaks his fast, and break it until it is said he never fasts.
When one who turns away from good things and desirable pleasures uses it, one who loves the finest things in the world, which are women and perfume, can use it.
When one who was gentle to his wives and lowered his wing to them uses it, one who disciplined them, hurt them, divorced, abandoned and gave them choice can use it.
When one who left personally engaging in the means of livelihood uses it, one who engaged in them personally can use it. He hired workers, hired himself out, bought, sold, borrowed, incurred debt and pledged.
When one who avoids women entirely during menstruation and fasting uses it, one who touches his wife while she is menstruating without intercourse, and one who kisses his wife while fasting, can use it.
When one who showed mercy to the people of sin because of destiny uses it, one who enforced the limits of Allah upon them, cutting off the thief's hand, stoning the adulterer and flogging the drinker, can use it.

He reported about the Prophet Allah's servant Solomon, peace be upon him, that he judged for the child to be the woman's, based on the apparent indicator, together with her acknowledgement of it to the other woman. He did not judge by the acknowledgement that had become apparent to him, because of the indicator that proved otherwise.
Abu Abd al-Rahman gave two chapter headings on this hadith. One is: "Latitude for the judge to say to a thing he does not do, 'Do it,' so that the truth may become clear." The other is: "Judgment contrary to what the one judged against acknowledges, when it becomes clear to the judge that the truth is other than what he acknowledged."
Likewise, the Companions acted on indicators during his lifetime and after him. Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, said to the woman who carried Hatib's letter: "Either you bring out the letter or I will strip you." Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, punished for fornication on the basis of pregnancy and for wine on the basis of its smell.
Allah, Glorified is He, related the account of the witness of Joseph, as a narrated statement that is not denied: that he judged by the indicator of the shirt torn from behind as proof of Joseph's innocence.
And he said to Ibn Abi al-Huqayq, when he claimed that expenditure had consumed the treasure of Huyayy ibn Akhtab: "The covenant is recent, and the wealth is more than that."

Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim)... 

He considered two indicators (qarinatayn) pointing to the continued possession of the wealth, and he punished him until he confessed to it.

And he permitted the relatives of the murdered person to swear against a man that he killed him, and to kill him in retaliation for it, based on the indicators that tip the balance in favour of their truthfulness. And God, glorified is He, prescribed the stoning of a woman when her husband testified against her in the case of li'an (mutual curse), and she refused to take the oath of li'an, because of the apparent indicator of his truthfulness.

His Sharia is replete with this for whoever reflects upon it. Judging by apparent indicators is from the very substance of His Sharia and what He brought, so it is a proof for the judges of truth and the rulers of justice, just as it is a proof against the judges of evil and the rulers of oppression. And God is the One sought for help.

The purpose of this section is that the patient poor are not more entitled to it (this) than the grateful rich, and the people most entitled to it are those most knowledgeable of His Sunnah and most following of it. And success is from God.

(Benefit)
He said to His Prophet: ﴿Say: I am not a novelty among the messengers, and I do not know what will be done with me or with you﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 9].

(Subtlety)
How great is the difference between the Messenger of Allah ﷺ being expelled from Makkah in that state, and his entry into it in that manner, which no human being has ever rejoiced in as he did for the sake of Allah. (Benefit)
His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, We have granted you a clear victory﴾.

The forgiveness of his past and future sins.
The completion of His blessing upon him.
His guidance to a straight path.
The victorious support of Allah for him, a mighty victory.

The answer is what we have mentioned: his acceptance of this decree, his contentment with it, his submission to it, and his entering under it, obliged Allah to give him that.

(Issue)
If it is asked: Why does the word [al-Sirat] (the path) come indefinite in His saying to His Prophet ﷺ: ﴿and guide you to a straight path﴾,
and His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And indeed, you guide to a straight path﴾, and His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And We chose them and guided them to a straight path﴾,
and His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Say: My Lord has guided me to a straight path﴾?
The answer to these instances is one answer: they are not in the context of supplication and request, but in the context of information from Allah, Exalted is He, about His guidance to a straight path and the guidance of His Messenger to it. The addressees had no prior acquaintance with it, and it was not known to them. Therefore it did not come definite with the definite article of prior reference, which points to something known in the mind of the addressee and present in his thoughts, nor was there any previously mentioned referent in the wording that would make the article known to him.
The definite article of prior reference comes in one of two cases: when there is a mentally known referent or a previous verbal mention. Since neither exists in these instances, indefiniteness is the basic form.
This is unlike His saying: ﴿Guide us to the straight path﴾. Since it was established among the addressees that Allah has a straight path to which He guided His prophets and messengers, and since the one addressed in the supplication, Glorified is He, knew it, the article was attached to it, and so He said: ﴿Guide us to the straight path﴾.
Al-Suhayli said: His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And guide you to a straight path﴾ was revealed concerning the treaty of al-Hudaybiyyah, when the Muslims disliked that treaty and considered that the right course was otherwise. Allah is exalted above what they say, and His Messenger ﷺ knew better. So Allah sent down this verse to His Messenger ﷺ. Thus it does not mean a straight path in religion, but a path in judgment, war and strategy.
As for His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And indeed, you guide to a straight path﴾,
that is, you guide from disbelief and misguidance to a straight path.
If He had said in this context "to the straight path," it would have given disbelief and misguidance a share of uprightness, since the definite article indicates that what it is attached to is more entitled to that meaning than what follows it in mention, or what is closer to it in the mind, and it is not entitled to it unless there is some part of it in the latter.
It is not hidden how weak and feeble these two answers are.
As for his claim that what is meant by His saying: ﴿and guide you to a straight path﴾ is in war and strategy, this diminishes this great favour and abundant portion with which Allah bestowed grace upon the Messenger ﷺ. The Prophet ﷺ informed that this verse was dearer to him than the world and all that is in it. When did Allah ever name war and strategy a straight path?
Has anyone, from the predecessors or the later scholars, interpreted this verse in that way? Rather, the straight path is what Allah placed upon it of guidance and the religion of truth, which He commanded him to report that Allah had guided him to, in His saying: ﴿Say: My Lord has guided me to a straight path﴾. Then He explained it with His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿a correct religion, the creed of Abraham, a man of pure faith, and he was not of those who associate others with Allah﴾. The word (religion) here is in the accusative as a substitute for the prepositional phrase, meaning: He guided me to a correct religion.
Can he then suppose here that war and strategy are meant? This answer is extremely corrupt.
Reflect: what Allah, Glorified is He, gathered for His Messenger in the verse of victory from kinds of gifts. They are five things:
The first: the clear victory.
The second: the forgiveness of his past and future sins.
The third: His guidance to the straight path.
The fourth: the completion of His blessing upon him.
The fifth: the bestowal of mighty victory. Glorified is He gathered for him between guidance and victory, because by these two foundations complete happiness and success are achieved. Guidance is knowledge of Allah, Exalted is He, and His religion, and acting in pursuit of His pleasure and obedience to Him. It is beneficial knowledge and righteous action. Victory is complete power to implement His religion: by proof, clarity, the sword and the spear. Victory is by proof and clarity, and by subduing the hearts of those who oppose him through proof, and subduing their bodies by the hand. Glorified is He often combines these two foundations, for by them the call is completed and His religion is made to prevail over all religion, as in His saying: ﴿It is He who sent His Messenger with guidance and the religion of truth﴾, in two places in Surat Bara'ah and in Surat al-Saff.
And He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿We sent Our messengers with clear evidences, and sent down with them the Book and the balance, that people may establish justice﴾. This is guidance.
Then He said: ﴿And We sent down iron, wherein is great might﴾. This is victory. So He mentioned the Book, the guide, and the iron, the helper.
And He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿Alif, Lam, Mim. Allah, there is no deity except Him, the Ever-Living, the Sustainer. He has sent down upon you, [O Muhammad], the Book in truth, confirming what was before it. And He revealed the Torah and the Gospel before, as guidance for the people, and He revealed the criterion﴾.
So He mentioned the sending down of the Book, the guide, and the Furqan, which is the victory that distinguishes between truth and falsehood.
The secret of linking victory with guidance is that each of them achieves the distinction between truth and falsehood. For this reason Exalted is He named what He gives His believing servants as victory a Furqan, as He said: ﴿If you have believed in Allah and in what We sent down upon Our servant on the Day of the Criterion, the day the two hosts met﴾.
So He mentioned both foundations: what He sent down upon His Messenger on the Day of the Furqan, which is the Day of Badr, the day on which Allah, Exalted is He, distinguished truth from falsehood by the victory of His Messenger and His religion and the humbling and disgrace of his enemies.
From this is His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And We certainly gave Moses and Aaron the criterion and a light and a reminder for the righteous﴾. So the Furqan was His support for him against Pharaoh and his people, and the light and the reminder were the Torah. This is the meaning of the verse. Whoever said that the waw is superfluous and that light is in the accusative as a state (ḥāl) has not been correct, as we have shown its error in "al-Amali al-Makkiyya." Thus it is clear that the verse of victory includes the two foundations, guidance and victory, and that nothing else is correct for it at all.
As for his second answer concerning His saying: ﴿And indeed, you guide to a straight path﴾, that if it were known it would give disbelief and misguidance a share of uprightness, I do not know where he got this understanding, despite his keen mind and wondrous understanding, may Allah have mercy on him. It is nothing but a stumble of a fine horse and a blunt sword's slip.
Do you suppose that His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And We gave them the clear Book and guided them to the straight path﴾ implies that others have a share of uprightness, when there is no other than the ways of misguidance? The straight path is one: it is what Allah, Exalted is He, guided all His prophets and messengers to, and it is the straight path, the path of those upon whom You have bestowed favour. Likewise, its definition in Surat al-Fatihah: does anyone say that it implies that others have a share of uprightness? Rather, it is said that its definition indicates that others have no share of uprightness, for the definite article is in the sense of restriction. It is as if it were said: the one with no straight path other than it. Understanding this restriction from the wording is stronger than understanding a share for others. So reflect on this here and in its counterparts.

Ibn al-Qayyim said, after some discussion:

The point is that since shirk (associating partners with God) is the greatest of injustices, the most abominable of abominations, and the most reprehensible of wrongs, it is the most hateful of things to God, the Exalted, the most detested by Him, and the most severely abhorred in His sight. He has attached to it punishments in this world and the next that He has not attached to any other sin. He declared that He will not forgive it, that its adherents are impure, and He forbade them from approaching His Sacred Precinct (al-Haram). He made their slaughtered animals and marriage with them unlawful, cut off allegiance between them and the believers, made them enemies of Him, of His angels, of His messengers and of the believers, and permitted the people of monotheism (tawhid) to take their wealth, their women and their children, and to enslave them. This is because shirk is a diminishing of the right of Lordship, a belittling of the majesty of Godhood, and an evil opinion of the Lord of the worlds, as God, the Exalted, said: ﴿And He will punish the hypocrite men and hypocrite women, and the polytheist men and polytheist women, who assume about God an assumption of evil. Upon them is a cycle of evil, and God has become angry with them and has cursed them and prepared for them Hell, and evil it is as a destination.﴾

No one has been subjected to a greater accumulation of threat and punishment than the people of shirk, for they held an evil opinion of Him, to the point that they associated others with Him. Had they held a good opinion of Him, they would have affirmed His oneness with its true affirmation.

Allah, glory be to Him, informed that He was pleased with the believers for entering under the pledge (bay'ah) to His Messenger. He knew what was in their hearts at that time of sincerity, fidelity, complete submission and obedience, and of preferring Allah and His Messenger over anything else. So Allah sent down tranquility (sakinah), serenity and contentment into their hearts, and rewarded them for being content with His judgment and patient with His command with a near victory (fath qarib) and many spoils that they would take. The first of the victories and spoils was the conquest of Khaybar and its spoils. Then the conquests and spoils continued until the end of time.

[The origin of the oaths of the pledge]

Among these obligations, which neither Allah nor His Messenger imposed on those who swear by them, are the oaths that the wicked tyrant al-Hajjaj ibn Yusuf arranged, namely the oaths of the pledge.

"The pledge in the time of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was by handshake, and the pledge of women was by speech. The noble hand of the Prophet (ﷺ) never touched the hand of a woman he did not own. He would say to the one pledging to him: 'I have pledged you,' or 'I pledge you,' upon hearing and obeying in hardship and ease, in what is pleasant and in what is disliked," as in the two Sahihs, from Ibn 'Umar: "We used to pledge to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to hear and obey, and he would say: 'As far as you are able.'" And in Sahih Muslim, from Jabir: "On the day of al-Hudaybiyah we were one thousand four hundred. We pledged to him while 'Umar was holding his hand under the tree. We pledged to him that we would not flee, and we did not pledge to him for death."

[How the Prophet's pledge to people was made]

In the two Sahihs, from 'Ubadah ibn al-Samit, who said: "We pledged to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to hear and obey in hardship and ease, in what is pleasant and what is disliked, and in being deprived of our share in favour of others, and that we would not dispute the matter with its people, and that we would speak the truth wherever we were, not fearing the blame of any blamer for the sake of Allah."

Also in the two Sahihs, from Junadah ibn Abi Umayyah, who said: "We entered upon 'Ubadah ibn al-Samit while he was ill, and we said: 'Narrate to us, may Allah set you right, a hadith from which we may benefit, that you heard from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).' He said: 'The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) called us and we pledged to him. Among what he took from us was that we pledged to him to hear and obey in what is pleasant and disliked, in hardship and ease, and in being deprived of our share in favour of others, and that we would not dispute the matter with its people, except that you see clear disbelief (kufr bawah) for which you have a proof from Allah.'"

Also in the two Sahihs, from 'A'ishah, who said: "When believing women emigrated to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), he would test them with the words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿O Prophet, when believing women come to you pledging to you that they will not associate anything with Allah, nor steal, nor commit adultery, nor kill their children...﴾ [al-Mumtahanah: 12] to the end of the verse."

'A'ishah said: "Whoever of the believing women affirmed this had affirmed the test. When they affirmed this in their words, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would say to them: 'Go, for I have pledged you.' By Allah, the hand of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) never touched the hand of any woman, but he pledged them by speech."

"'A'ishah said: 'By Allah, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) never took a pledge from women except with what Allah commanded him, and the palm of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) never touched the palm of any woman. When he took their pledge he would say to them: "I have pledged you" by word alone.'"

This is the prophetic pledge about which Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿Indeed, those who pledge allegiance to you, they are actually pledging allegiance to Allah. The hand of Allah is over their hands. So whoever breaks his pledge only breaks it to his own detriment, and whoever fulfils what he has covenanted with Allah, He will give him a great reward.﴾ [al-Fath: 10] and He said about it: ﴿Certainly, Allah was pleased with the believers when they pledged allegiance to you under the tree.﴾ [al-Fath: 18]

[The oaths of the pledge that al-Hajjaj al-Thaqafi introduced]

Then al-Hajjaj introduced into Islam a pledge other than this, which includes swearing by Allah, the Exalted, divorce, manumission, giving charity of wealth, and Hajj. The scholars of Islam differed over this in several opinions. We will mention the clarification and explanation of this question. If the swearer's intention by his saying "The oaths of the pledge bind me" is the prophetic pledge upon which the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) pledged his companions, then divorce, manumission and nothing of what al-Hajjaj arranged binds him. If he does not intend that pledge but intends the Hajjaj pledge, then he is in one of these situations: either he mentions in his words divorce, manumission, Hajj, charity or an oath by Allah, or he mentions none of these. If he mentions none of them in his words, then he either knows its content or does not. In either case, he either intends all of its content, or some of what is in it, or intends none of that. These are the divisions of this question.

[Chapter: Knowledge, forbearance, dignity and tranquility]

As for his saying: "that he has forbearance (hilm), dignity (waqar) and tranquility (sakinah)":

The person of knowledge and giving fatwa has no greater need for anything than for forbearance, tranquility and dignity, for these are the garment of his knowledge and its beauty. If he lacks them, his knowledge is like a naked body without clothing.

Some of the early pious predecessors (salaf) said: "Nothing is joined to anything better than knowledge joined to forbearance."

People here are of four kinds. The best of them are those given both forbearance and knowledge, and the worst of them are those lacking both. The third are those given knowledge without forbearance, and the fourth is the reverse. Forbearance is the adornment, splendour and beauty of knowledge.

The opposite of forbearance is recklessness, haste, hot-temperedness, rashness and lack of steadiness. The forbearing person is not provoked by hasty impulses, is not belittled by the ignorant, and is not disturbed by people of recklessness, levity and ignorance.

Rather, he is dignified, steady, and possessed of patience. He controls himself when the first things come upon him and they do not control him. His regard for consequences prevents him from being carried away by the motives of anger and desire. Through knowledge, the places of good and evil, righteousness and corruption are revealed to him, and through forbearance he is able to firm his soul in the face of good, so that he prefers it and perseveres in it, and in the face of evil, so that he remains patient and refrains from it. Knowledge makes his right course known to him, and forbearance keeps him firm upon it. If you wish to see one who is discerning of good and evil yet has no patience to act upon this or refrain from that, you will see him. If you wish to see one who is patient through hardships yet lacks insight, you will see him. If you wish to see one who has neither patience nor insight, you will see him. And if you wish to see one who is insightful and patient, you will hardly find him. When you see him, you have seen a true imam of guidance, so hold fast to his stirrup.

Dignity and tranquility are the fruit and result of forbearance.

Because of the great need for tranquility, its reality, details and divisions, we will indicate these according to our limited knowledge, our rigid minds and our deficient expressions. But we are the children of our time, and people resemble their time more than their fathers, and every age has its dynasty and its men.

[The reality of tranquility]

Sakinah is a form (fa'ilah) derived from sukun, which is the calm and settling of the heart. Its origin is in the heart, and its effect appears upon the limbs. It is of two kinds: general and specific.

The tranquility of the Prophets, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon them, is the most specific of its ranks and the highest of its categories, such as the tranquility that came to Abraham the Friend when he was thrown into the catapult, travelling toward the fire that Allah's enemies had kindled for him. So to Allah belongs that tranquility which was in his heart at that moment. Likewise the tranquility that came to Moses when Pharaoh and his armies pursued him from behind, with the sea before them, while the Children of Israel cried out: "O Moses, where are you taking us? This sea is before us and this Pharaoh is behind us." Likewise the tranquility that came to him at the time of Allah speaking to him, a call and a whisper, a speech in truth that he heard in reality with his own ear. Likewise the tranquility that came to him when he saw the staff become a manifest serpent, and likewise the tranquility that descended upon him when he saw the ropes and staffs of the people as though they were moving, so he sensed fear within himself. Likewise the tranquility that came to our Prophet (ﷺ) when his enemy overlooked him and his companion while they were in the cave, and if one of them had looked down at his feet he would have seen them. Likewise the tranquility that descended upon him in his great stands, when Allah's enemies surrounded him, such as the Day of Badr, the Day of Hunayn, the Day of the Trench and others. This tranquility is a matter beyond human intellects, and it is among the greatest of his miracles in the view of those of insight. For the liar, especially against Allah, is at his most anxious, most fearful and most agitated in such situations. So if the Messengers, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon them, had no sign except this alone, it would have sufficed them.

[Specific tranquility]

As for the specific tranquility, it belongs to the followers of the Messengers according to their following. It is the tranquility of faith, a tranquility that calms hearts from doubt and suspicion. For this reason Allah sent it down upon the believers in the most difficult situations, when they most needed it: ﴿It is He who sent down tranquility into the hearts of the believers so that they might increase in faith along with their faith. And to Allah belong the armies of the heavens and the earth, and Allah is ever Knowing and Wise.﴾ [al-Fath: 4]

So He mentioned His favour upon them through the armies outside them and the armies within them, which is the tranquility at the time of anxiety and agitation that someone like 'Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him) could not bear, and that was on the day of al-Hudaybiyah. Allah, Glorified and Exalted, mentioned His favour upon them by sending it down when they needed it most: ﴿Certainly, Allah was pleased with the believers when they pledged allegiance to you under the tree, so He knew what was in their hearts, and He sent down tranquility upon them and rewarded them with a near victory.﴾ [al-Fath: 18]

When Allah, Glorified and Exalted, knew the anxiety and agitation in their hearts, when the disbelievers of Quraysh prevented them from entering the House of Allah, held back the sacrificial animals from their place of sacrifice, and imposed upon them those unjust and oppressive conditions, their hearts were agitated and disturbed, and they could not bear patience. So He, Exalted, knew what was in them and firmed them with tranquility, out of His mercy, compassion and kindness. He is the Subtle, the All-Aware.

The verse may also bear another meaning: that He, Glorified, knew what was in their hearts of faith, goodness and love for it and for His Messenger, so He firmed them with tranquility at the time of their disturbance and agitation. The apparent meaning is that the verse encompasses both matters: He knew what was in their hearts of what required sending down tranquility, and the good in their hearts that was the cause of its sending down. Then He said after that: ﴿When those who disbelieved put into their hearts zealotry, the zealotry of ignorance, then Allah sent down His tranquility upon His Messenger and upon the believers, and He made them adhere to the word of piety, and they were more deserving of it and worthy of it. And Allah is ever Knowing of all things.﴾ [al-Fath: 26]

When the zealotry of ignorance necessitates sayings and actions that suit it, Allah placed in the hearts of His allies a tranquility that opposes the zealotry of ignorance, and on their tongues the word of piety, opposing what the zealotry of ignorance necessitates of the word of immorality. So the share of the believers was tranquility in their hearts and the word of piety on their tongues, and the share of their enemies was the zealotry of ignorance in their hearts and the word of immorality and transgression on their tongues. This tranquility and this word were thus a host from the armies of Allah, with which Allah strengthened His Messenger and the believers against the army of Satan that is in the hearts and on the tongues of his allies.

The fruit of this tranquility is calm assurance (tuma'ninah) toward good, through affirmation and certainty, and submission and compliance toward the command. So it does not leave any doubt opposing the good, nor any desire opposing the command. Evil objections do not pass through the heart except that they are only passing by the satanic whisperings with which the servant is tested, so that his faith may grow strong and his standing with Allah may be raised, by repelling them, rejecting them and not inclining toward them. The believer should not think that they are due to a deficiency in his rank with Allah.

[Section: Tranquility at performing the duties of servitude]

**Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 48, verse 18 (part 2 of 5):**

Among its fruits is *sakinah* (tranquility) during the performance of the duties of servitude (*'ubudiyyah*). It produces humility (*khudu'*), submissiveness (*khushu'*), lowering the gaze, and the gathering of the heart upon Allah, the Exalted, such that the servant performs his servitude with his heart and body. *Khushu'* is the result and fruit of this tranquility, and the humility of the limbs is the result of the humility of the heart. The Prophet (ﷺ) saw a man fidgeting with his beard during prayer, and he said: "If this man's heart were humble, his limbs would be humble."

If you say: You have mentioned its divisions, its result, its fruit, and its sign, so what are its causes that bring it about?

[Causes of Tranquility]

I say: Its cause is the dominance of the servant's *muraqabah* (vigilant awareness) of his Lord, may His majesty be exalted, to the point that it is as though he sees Him. The more intense this *muraqabah* is, the more it necessitates for him modesty (*haya'*), tranquility, love (*mahabbah*), submissiveness, humility, fear (*khawf*), and hope (*raja'*), which cannot be attained without it. Thus *muraqabah* is the foundation of all the deeds of the heart and its pillar upon which they stand. The Prophet (ﷺ) gathered the roots of the deeds of the heart and all their branches in a single phrase, namely his words concerning *ihsan* (excellence): "That you worship Allah as if you see Him." So reflect on every station (*maqam*) of religion and every deed of the heart: how you find that this is its root and source.

The point is that the servant needs tranquility when doubts arise that challenge the foundations of faith, so that his heart remains firm and does not deviate. He needs it when doubts and thoughts arise that undermine the works of faith, lest they grow stronger and become worries, griefs, and desires by which his faith diminishes. He needs it when the causes of fear, of various kinds, arise, so that his heart remains steady and his composure is preserved. He needs it when the causes of joy arise, lest his mount run away with him and he exceed the limit that must not be crossed, so that joy turns into distress and sorrow. How many are those upon whom Allah bestows what gladdens them, yet the mount of joy runs away with them and they exceed the limit, so that it quickly turns into distress. Had they been given tranquility equal to their joy, the good would have been intended for them. And success is from Allah. He needs it when painful matters descend upon him, of various kinds, apparent and hidden. How greatly he needs tranquility at such a time, how beneficial it is for him, how useful it is to him, and how good its outcome is.

Tranquility in these situations is a sign of victory, of attaining what is loved, and of the removal of what is hated; its absence is a sign of the opposite. Neither of these signs errs. And Allah is the One sought for help.

[Section: On the Story of al-Hudaybiyyah]

Nafi' said: It was in the sixth year, in Dhu al-Qa'dah. This is the correct view, and it is the view of al-Zuhri, Qatadah, Musa ibn 'Uqbah, Muhammad ibn Ishaq, and others.

Hisham ibn 'Urwah said, on the authority of his father: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) went out to al-Hudaybiyyah in Ramadan, whereas it was in Shawwal. This is an error. The Conquest campaign was in Ramadan. Abu al-Aswad also said, on the authority of 'Urwah, that it was in Dhu al-Qa'dah, and this is correct.

In the *Sahihayn* (the two Sahih collections), on the authority of Anas, that the Prophet (ﷺ) "performed four 'umrahs, all of them in Dhu al-Qa'dah."

He mentioned among them the 'umrah of al-Hudaybiyyah.

With him were one thousand five hundred. This is as stated in the *Sahihayn* on the authority of Jabir. And from him, in both (collections): "They were one thousand four hundred." And in both, on the authority of 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Awfa: "We were one thousand three hundred."

Qatadah said: I said to Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib: How many were those who witnessed the Pledge of Ridwan? He said: Fifteen hundred. I said: Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah said they were fourteen hundred. He said: May Allah have mercy on him; he erred. He himself told me they were fifteen hundred.

I say: Two statements have been authenticated from Jabir. It has also been authenticated from him that they slaughtered seventy camels in the year of al-Hudaybiyyah, with each camel counting for seven. He was asked: How many were you? He said: One thousand four hundred, with our horsemen and our infantry.

That is, the cavalry and infantry among them. The heart inclines to this view, and it is the view of al-Bara' ibn 'Azib, Ma'qil ibn Yasar, and Salamah ibn al-Akwa' in the more authentic of the two narrations.

And there is the statement of al-Musayyib ibn Hazn. Shu'bah said, on the authority of Qatadah, on the authority of Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, on the authority of his father: "We were with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) under the tree, one thousand four hundred."

Whoever said they were seven hundred erred a clear error. His excuse is that they slaughtered seventy camels that day, and a camel has been reported to suffice for seven and for ten. But this does not support what that speaker said, for he himself stated that the camel in this 'umrah was for seven. If the seventy had been for all of them, they would have been four hundred and ninety men. And in the same narration's completion he said that they "were one thousand four hundred."

[Section: On His (ﷺ) Garlanding the Sacrificial Animals at Dhu al-Hulayfah and Sending Ibn Khuza'ah as a Spy to Quraysh]

"When they were at Dhu al-Hulayfah, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) garlanded the sacrificial animals (*hady*) and marked them, and he entered the state of ihram for 'umrah. He sent ahead of him a spy of his from Khuza'ah, who would inform him about Quraysh. When he was near 'Usfan, his spy came to him and said: 'I have left Ka'b ibn Lu'ayy, who have gathered the Ahabish for you, and have gathered armies for you. They will fight you, bar you from the House, and prevent you.' The Prophet (ﷺ) consulted his companions and said: 'Do you see that we should turn toward the offspring of those who assisted them, and seize them? If they remain seated, they will remain seated as those who have been bereaved and defeated. And if they come, it will be a neck which Allah has cut off. Or do you see that we should head for the House, and whoever bars us from it, we fight him?'

Abu Bakr said: 'Allah and His Messenger know best. We came as 'umrah pilgrims, and we did not come to fight anyone. But whoever stands between us and the House, we will fight him.' The Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'Then proceed.' So they proceeded, until when they were in part of the way, the Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'Khalid ibn al-Walid is at al-Ghamim with cavalry of Quraysh as a vanguard, so take the right side.'

By Allah, Khalid did not perceive them until he saw the dust of the army. He ran off as a warner to Quraysh. The Prophet (ﷺ) continued until, when he reached the mountain pass by which they would descend upon them, his she-camel knelt down with him. The people said: 'Hal, hal!' But she did not rise. They said: 'al-Qaswa' has stopped, al-Qaswa' has stopped!' The Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'Al-Qaswa' has not stopped, nor is that her habit, but the One who stopped the elephant has stopped her.'

Then he said: 'By Him in whose hand is my soul, they will not ask me for any arrangement in which they honor the sanctities of Allah, except that I will give it to them.' Then he urged her on, and she sprang up with him. He turned aside until he halted at the farthest part of al-Hudaybiyyah, at a small pool of water, from which people could only take a little at a time. The people soon drained it, and they complained to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) of thirst. He drew an arrow from his quiver and commanded them to put it in the pool. He said: 'By Allah, it continued to gush forth water for them until they departed from it.'

Quraysh was alarmed at his descent upon them, so the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) wished to send a man from among his companions to them. He called 'Umar ibn al-Khattab to send him. He said: 'O Messenger of Allah, there is no one from the clan of Ka'b in Makkah who would become angry for me if I were harmed. So send 'Uthman ibn 'Affan, for his tribe is there, and he will convey what you intend.' The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) called 'Uthman ibn 'Affan and sent him to Quraysh, saying: 'Inform them that we did not come to fight, but came only as 'umrah pilgrims, and invite them to Islam.' He commanded him to go to men in Makkah who were believers and to women who were believers, to enter upon them, to give them glad tidings of victory, and to inform them that Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, will make His religion prevail in Makkah, so that faith will no longer have to be concealed there.

'Uthman set out and passed by Quraysh at Baldah. They said: 'Where are you headed?' He said: 'The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) has sent me to invite you to Allah and to Islam, and to inform you that we did not come to fight, but only came as 'umrah pilgrims.' They said: 'We have heard what you say; proceed with your need.' Aban ibn Sa'id ibn al-'As stood up to him, welcomed him, and saddled his horse. He mounted 'Uthman on the horse and gave him protection, and Aban rode behind him until he reached Makkah.

Before 'Uthman returned, the Muslims said: ''Uthman has reached the House before us and circumambulated it.' The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'I do not think he has circumambulated the House while we are besieged.' They said: 'What would prevent him, O Messenger of Allah, now that he has reached it?' He said: 'That is my assumption about him: that he will not circumambulate the Ka'bah until we circumambulate it with him.'"

"The Muslims mixed with the polytheists regarding the matter of the truce. A man from one of the two groups threw a stone at a man from the other group, and it became a battle. They shot at each other with arrows and stones, and both groups cried out. Each group took captives from the other. News reached the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that 'Uthman had been killed. So he called for the pledge of allegiance, and the Muslims rushed to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who was under the tree, and they pledged allegiance to him that they would not flee. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) took hold of his own hand and said: 'This is on behalf of 'Uthman.' When the pledge was complete, 'Uthman returned, and the Muslims said to him: 'Have you satisfied yourself, O Abu 'Abd Allah, with circumambulating the House?'

He said: 'Evil is what you thought of me. By Him in whose hand is my soul, even if I had remained there a year while the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was staying at al-Hudaybiyyah, I would not have circumambulated it until the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) circumambulated it. Quraysh invited me to circumambulate the House, but I refused.'

The Muslims said: 'The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was the most knowledgeable of us about Allah and the best of us in opinion.' ['Umar was holding the hand of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) for the pledge under the tree, and all the Muslims pledged allegiance to him except al-Jadd ibn Qays.] [Ma'qil ibn Yasar was holding one of its branches, raising it away from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). The first to pledge allegiance to him was Abu Sinan al-Asadi.]

Salamah ibn al-Akwa' pledged allegiance to him three times, at the beginning, middle, and end of the people.

While they were in that state, Budayl ibn Warqa' al-Khuza'i came with a group from Khuza'ah. They were the confidants of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) from the people of Tihamah. He said: 'I have left Ka'b ibn Lu'ayy and 'Amir ibn Lu'ayy, who have camped at the springs of al-Hudaybiyyah, with them the nursing she-camels with their young. They will fight you and bar you from the House.'

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'We did not come to fight anyone, but we came as 'umrah pilgrims. Quraysh has been exhausted by war and harmed by it. If they wish, I will make a truce with them, and they will leave me and the people alone. And if they wish to enter what the people have entered, they may do so. Otherwise, they will have gathered their strength. But if they refuse except to fight, then by Him in whose hand is my soul, I will fight them for this affair of mine until my neck is severed, or Allah will surely make His command prevail.'

Budayl said: 'I will convey to them what you say.' He set out until he came to Quraysh and said: 'I have come to you from this man, and I heard him say a statement. If you wish, I will present it to you.' Their foolish ones said: 'We have no need for you to tell us anything about him.' But those of judgment among them said: 'Tell us what you heard.' He said: 'I heard him say such and such,' and he related to them what the Prophet (ﷺ) had said.

'Urwah ibn Mas'ud al-Thaqafi said: 'This man has presented you with a proposal of right guidance, so accept it, and let me go to him.' They said: 'Go to him.' So he came to him and began speaking with him. The Prophet (ﷺ) said to him something similar to what he had said to Budayl. 'Urwah then said: 'O Muhammad, tell me: if you destroy your own people, have you ever heard of anyone among the Arabs who has destroyed his own family before you? And if the other outcome occurs, then by Allah, I see faces, and I see a rabble of people who I think will flee and abandon you.'

Abu Bakr said to him: 'Suck the clitoris of al-Lat! Do we flee from him and abandon him?!' He said: 'Who is this?' They said: 'Abu Bakr.' He said: 'As for Him in whose hand is my soul, were it not for a favor you had upon me, which I have not yet repaid, I would have answered you.'

He kept speaking with the Prophet (ﷺ), and every time he spoke he would take hold of his beard. Al-Mughirah ibn Shu'bah was at the head of the Prophet (ﷺ), with a sword and wearing a helmet. Whenever 'Urwah reached out toward the beard of the Prophet (ﷺ), he would strike his hand with the back of the sword and say: 'Keep your hand away from the beard of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).' 'Urwah raised his head and said: 'Who is this?' They said: 'al-Mughirah ibn Shu'bah.'

He said: 'You treacherous one! Am I not trying to repair your treachery?' Al-Mughirah had accompanied a group of people in the pre-Islamic period, killed them, took their wealth, and then came and embraced Islam. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'As for Islam, I accept it. As for the wealth, I have no share in it whatsoever.'

Then ʿUrwa began to look at the Companions of the Messenger of God ﷺ with his eyes. By God, whenever the Prophet ﷺ spat, his spittle would fall into the palm of one of them, and he would rub it over his skin and face. When he commanded them, they hastened to carry out his command; when he performed ablution, they nearly fought over his ablution water; and when he spoke, they lowered their voices in his presence, and they did not stare at him intently, out of reverence for him. So ʿUrwa returned to his companions and said: "O my people, by God, I have been received by kings: by Kisra, Caesar and the Negus. By God, I have never seen a king whom his companions revere as much as Muhammad's companions revere Muhammad. By God, if he spits a gob of phlegm, it falls into the palm of one of them, and he rubs it over his face and skin. When he commands them, they hasten to carry out his command; when he performs ablution, they nearly fight over his ablution water; and when he speaks, they lower their voices in his presence, and they do not stare at him intently out of reverence for him. He has offered you a sound course, so accept it."

A man from the Banu Kinana said: "Let me go to him." They said: "Go to him." When he came in sight of the Prophet ﷺ and his Companions, the Messenger of God ﷺ said: "This is so-and-so, and he is from a people who honour the sacrificial camels, so send them to him." They sent them to him, and the people met him reciting the talbiya. When he saw this, he said: "Glory be to God! It is not fitting that these people be barred from the House." He returned to his companions and said: "I saw that the camels had been garlanded and marked, and I do not think they should be barred from the House." Then Mikraz ibn Hafs stood up and said: "Let me go to him." They said: "Go to him." When he came in sight of them, the Prophet ﷺ said: "This is Mikraz ibn Hafs, and he is a wicked man."

So he began speaking with the Messenger of God ﷺ, and while he was speaking to him, Suhayl ibn ʿAmr arrived. The Prophet ﷺ said: "Your affair has been made easy for you." Suhayl said: "Come, write a document between us and you."

He summoned the scribe and said: "Write: In the name of God, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate." Suhayl said: "As for 'the Most Merciful', by God we do not know what it is. Rather, write: 'In Your name, O God, as you used to write.'" The Muslims said: "By God, we will not write it except as 'In the name of God, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate.'" The Prophet ﷺ said: "Write: 'In Your name, O God.'"

Then he said: "Write: This is what Muhammad, the Messenger of God, has agreed to." Suhayl said: "By God, if we knew that you were the Messenger of God, we would not have barred you from the House or fought you. Rather, write: Muhammad ibn ʿAbdullah." The Prophet ﷺ said: "I am the Messenger of God, even if you deny me. Write: Muhammad ibn ʿAbdullah." The Prophet ﷺ then said: "On condition that you leave us free between us and the House, so that we may circumambulate it."

Suhayl said: "By God, the Arabs must not say that we were subjected to coercion; but that will be in the coming year." So it was written. Suhayl said: "On condition that no man from us comes to you, even if he is upon your religion, except that you return him to us."

The Muslims said: "Glory be to God! How can he be returned to the polytheists when he has come as a Muslim?!" While they were in this state, Abu Jandal ibn Suhayl ibn ʿAmr came, dragging his feet in his shackles, having come out from the lower part of Mecca until he threw himself in the midst of the Muslims. Suhayl said: "This, O Muhammad, is the first thing I make a condition of our agreement: that you return him to me." The Prophet ﷺ said: "We have not yet concluded the document."

He said: "By God, then I will never make peace with you over anything at all." The Prophet ﷺ said: "Then permit him for me." He said: "I will not permit him for you." He said: "Yes, do so." He said: "I will not do so." Mikraz said: "Yes, indeed, we have permitted him." Abu Jandal said: "O assembly of Muslims, I am being returned to the polytheists when I have come as a Muslim. Do you not see what I have suffered?!"

He had been severely tortured for the sake of God.

ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab said: "By God, I have had no doubt since I embraced Islam except on that day. So I came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: 'O Messenger of God, are you not truly the Prophet of God?' He said: 'Yes.'

I said: 'Are we not upon the truth and our enemy upon falsehood?' He said: 'Yes.'

I said: 'Why then should we accept humiliation in our religion, and return while God has not yet judged between us and our enemies?' He said: 'I am the Messenger of God, and He is my helper, and I do not disobey Him.' I said: 'Did you not used to tell us that we would come to the House and circumambulate it?' He said: 'Yes. But did I inform you that you would come to it this year?' I said: 'No.' He said: 'Then you will come to it and circumambulate it.'"

ʿUmar said: "So I came to Abu Bakr and said to him what I had said to the Messenger of God ﷺ. Abu Bakr replied to me just as the Messenger of God ﷺ had replied, and added: 'Hold fast to his stirrup until you die, for by God, he is upon the truth.'"

ʿUmar said: "So I did certain deeds for that reason."

When the matter of the document was concluded, the Messenger of God ﷺ said: "Rise, slaughter, then shave your heads."

By God, not one man among them rose until he had said this three times. When none of them rose, he got up and entered upon Umm Salama and told her what he had encountered from the people. Umm Salama said: "O Messenger of God, do you wish for this? Go out, and do not speak to any of them a word until you slaughter your camel and call your barber, and he shaves you." So he rose, went out, and did not speak to any of them until he had done this: he slaughtered his camel and called his barber, who shaved him. When the people saw this, they rose and slaughtered, and some of them began shaving others, until some of them nearly killed others out of grief. Then believing women came to him, and God, mighty and majestic, revealed: ﴿O you who have believed, when believing women come to you as emigrants, test them﴾ [al-Mumtahana: 10], until He reached ﴿the disbelieving wives﴾. On that day ʿUmar divorced two women who had been his wives in polytheism; one of them was married by Muʿawiya, and the other by Safwan ibn Umayya. Then he returned to Medina, and on his return God revealed to him: ﴿Indeed We have granted you a clear victory, that God may forgive you your past and future sins, complete His favour upon you, guide you to a straight path, and help you with mighty help﴾.

ʿUmar said: "Is it a victory, O Messenger of God?" He said: "Yes." The Companions said: "Congratulations to you, O Messenger of God; but what is for us?" So God, mighty and majestic, revealed: ﴿It is He who sent down tranquillity into the hearts of the believers﴾.

When he returned to Medina, Abu Basir, a man of Quraysh, came to him as a Muslim. They sent two men to seek him, saying: "The covenant you made with us." So he handed him over to the two men, and they set out with him until they reached Dhu al-Hulayfa, where they dismounted and ate some dates they had. Abu Basir said to one of the two men: "By God, I think your sword is good." The other drew it and said: "Yes, by God, it is indeed good; I have tested it many times."

Abu Basir said: "Show it to me, let me look at it." So he gave it to him, and he struck him with it until he was dead, and the other fled running until he reached Medina, entered the mosque. The Messenger of God ﷺ said, when he saw him: "This one has seen terror."

When he reached the Prophet ﷺ, he said: "By God, my companion has been killed, and I am about to be killed." Then Abu Basir came and said: "O Prophet of God, by God, God has fulfilled your covenant. You returned me to them, and God delivered me from them."

The Prophet ﷺ said: "Woe to his mother! He is a kindler of war; if only he had someone with him." When he heard that, he understood that he would return him to them, so he went out until he reached the coast at Sif al-Bahr. Abu Jandal ibn Suhayl escaped from them and joined Abu Basir, and no man of Quraysh who had embraced Islam went out without joining Abu Basir, until a band of them gathered. By God, they did not hear of a caravan of Quraysh going to Syria without intercepting it, killing them and taking their property. So Quraysh sent to the Prophet ﷺ, appealing to him by God and kinship, that he should send for them, and whoever came to him from them would be safe. Then God, mighty and majestic, revealed: ﴿It is He who restrained their hands from you and your hands from them in the heart of Mecca, after He had given you victory over them﴾ [al-Fath: 24], until ﴿the zealotry of the age of ignorance﴾ [al-Fath: 26]. Their zealotry was that they did not acknowledge that he was the Prophet of God, nor did they acknowledge "In the name of God, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate," and they barred between them and the House.

I say: In the Sahih it is reported that the Prophet ﷺ performed ablution and spat from his mouth into the well of al-Hudaybiya, and its water gushed forth. Likewise al-Bara ibn ʿAzib and Salama ibn al-Akwaʿ related this in the two Sahihs.

ʿUrwa said, on the authority of Marwan ibn al-Hakam and al-Miswar ibn Makhrama, that he planted an arrow from his quiver in it. This is also in the two Sahihs.

In the Maghazi of Abu al-Aswad, on the authority of ʿUrwa: he performed ablution in a bucket, rinsed his mouth, then spat into it, and ordered that it be poured into the well. He drew an arrow from his quiver and cast it into the well, and invoked God, the Exalted, and it bubbled with water, until they began scooping water with their hands while they sat on its edge. Thus he combined the two accounts, and this is more likely. And God knows best.

In Sahih al-Bukhari, on the authority of Jabir, who said: "The people became thirsty on the day of al-Hudaybiya, while the Messenger of God ﷺ had before him a small vessel from which he performed ablution. The people surged toward him, and he said: 'What is the matter with you?' They said: 'O Messenger of God, we have no water to drink or to perform ablution with, except what is before you.' So he placed his hand in the vessel, and water began to gush forth from between his fingers like springs. They drank and performed ablution, and they were fifteen hundred."

This is other than the story of the well.

During this campaign, rain fell on them one night. When the Prophet ﷺ had led the dawn prayer, he said: "Do you know what your Lord said last night?" They said: "God and His Messenger know best." He said: "Some of My servants have awoken as believers in Me and some as disbelievers. As for the one who said: 'We have been given rain by the grace and mercy of God,' he is a believer in Me and a disbeliever in the star. As for the one who said: 'We have been given rain by such-and-such a constellation,' he is a disbeliever in Me and a believer in the star."

[Section on what the treaty of al-Hudaybiya stipulated]

The peace between the Muslims and the people of Mecca was concluded on laying down arms for ten years, that people would be safe from one another, and that he would withdraw from them that year; and that when the next year came, he would come and they would vacate between him and Mecca, so that he might stay there three days; that he would not enter it except with the weapons of a rider, with swords in their sheaths; that whoever came to us from your companions we would not return to you, and whoever came to you from our companions you would return to us; and that between us and you there is a sealed chest, and that there shall be no theft and no betrayal. They said: "O Messenger of God, shall we give them this?" He said: "Whoever comes to them from us, God will remove him far away; and whoever comes to us from them, we will return him to them, and God will make for him a way out and a means of relief."

In the story of al-Hudaybiya, God, mighty and majestic, revealed the ransom for harm for one who shaves his head, by fasting, almsgiving or a sacrifice, concerning Kaʿb ibn ʿUjra.

In it the Messenger of God ﷺ prayed for forgiveness for those who shaved their heads three times, and once for those who shortened their hair.

In it they slaughtered a camel for seven and a cow for seven.

In it the Messenger of God ﷺ sent as part of his offering a camel that had belonged to Abu Jahl, which had a silver ring in its nose, in order to enrage the polytheists.

In it Surat al-Fath was revealed. Khuza'a entered into the pact and covenant of the Messenger of God ﷺ, and Banu Bakr entered into the pact and covenant of Quraysh. The condition was that whoever wished to enter into the pact of the Prophet ﷺ might do so, and whoever wished to enter into the pact of Quraysh might do so.

When he returned to Medina, believing women came to him, among them Umm Kulthum bint ʿUqba ibn Abi Muʿayt. Her family came asking the Messenger of God ﷺ to return her according to the condition that had been between them, but he did not return her to them, and God, mighty and majestic, forbade him to do so.

It was said: this is an abrogation of the condition concerning women.

It was also said: it is a specification of the Sunna by the Qur'an, and this is very rare.

It was also said: the condition applied only to men specifically, and the polytheists wished to extend it to both categories, but God refused that.

[Section: some of the jurisprudential benefits in the story of al-Hudaybiya]

Among them: the Prophet ﷺ performed ʿUmra in the months of Hajj, for he set out for it in Dhu al-Qaʿda.

Among them: that entering ihram for ʿUmra from the miqat is better, just as entering ihram for Hajj is likewise; for he entered ihram for both from Dhu al-Hulayfa, which is about a mile or so from Medina. As for the hadith, "Whoever enters ihram for ʿUmra from Bayt al-Maqdis, his past and future sins will be forgiven," and in another wording, "It will be an expiation for what preceded it of sins," this is a hadith that is not authentic, and its chain and text have been subject to severe inconsistency.

Among them: that driving the sacrificial animal is recommended in a solitary ʿUmra just as it is recommended in Qiran.

**Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 48, verse 18 (part 4 of 5):**

Among its lessons: the marking of the sacrificial animal (*ish'ār al-hady*, marking the animal so it is recognized as an offering) is a Sunnah and not a prohibited mutilation (*muthla*).

Among its lessons: it is recommended to enrage the enemies of Allah. The Prophet (ﷺ) sent, among his sacrificial animals, a camel for Abu Jahl with a silver ring in its nose, to enrage the polytheists. Allah, the Exalted, said describing the Prophet (ﷺ) and his companions: ﴿And their likeness in the Gospel is as a seed which sends forth its shoot and strengthens it, so it grows firm and stands upon its stalk, pleasing the sowers, that He may enrage the disbelievers by them﴾ [al-Fath: 29].

And He, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿That is because they are not afflicted with thirst or fatigue or hunger in the way of Allah, nor do they tread any path that enrages the disbelievers, nor do they inflict on an enemy any harm except that a righteous deed is recorded for them thereby. Indeed, Allah does not waste the reward of the doers of good﴾ [al-Tawbah: 120].

Among its lessons: the commander of an army should send scouts (*'uyūn*, singular *'ayn*) ahead of him toward the enemy.

Among its lessons: seeking help from a trustworthy polytheist in jihad is permissible when there is need, because the spy, the man from Khuzā'ah, was a disbeliever at that time. It also has the benefit that he is closer to mixing with the enemy and gathering their news.

Among its lessons: it is recommended for the leader (*imam*) to consult his subjects and his army, in order to draw out the best opinion, to please their hearts, to secure them against resentment, and to learn of an interest that some of them know and others do not, and in obedience to the Lord's command in His saying: ﴿And consult them in the matter﴾ [Al 'Imran: 159].

Allah, glorified and exalted, has praised His servants by His saying: ﴿and whose affair is by consultation among themselves﴾ [al-Shura: 38].

Among its lessons: it is permissible to take captive the offspring of the polytheists if they are separated from their men before the men are fought.

Among its lessons: rejecting false speech, even when it is attributed to one who is not legally accountable. When they said, "al-Qaswa' has balked," meaning she became stubborn and insisted and did not proceed, and *al-khilā'* in camels, with a kasra on the kha and a long vowel, is the equivalent of *al-himrān* in horses, when they attributed to the she-camel what is not of her nature and disposition, he rejected it from them and said:

"She did not balk, nor is that her nature."

Then he (ﷺ) informed them of the reason for her kneeling, and that the One who held back the elephant from Makkah held her back for the great wisdom that became evident through her being held back and what followed after it.

Among its lessons: naming what a man rides or uses of his mounts and the like is a Sunnah.

Among its lessons: it is permissible to swear, and indeed recommended, upon a religious report one wishes to affirm. It is transmitted from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he swore oaths in more than eighty places. And Allah, the Exalted, commanded him to swear to confirm what he reported in three places: in (Surah Yunus), (Saba') and (al-Taghabun).

Among its lessons: when polytheists, people of innovation, the immoral, rebels, and oppressors ask for a matter in which they honor one of the sacred prohibitions of Allah, the Exalted, they are answered, given what they ask, and assisted in it. If they prevent others from it, they are still helped in what contains the glorification of the sacred prohibitions of Allah, the Exalted, not in their disbelief or their transgression, and they are prevented from anything other than that. So whoever seeks help in what is beloved to Allah, the Exalted, and pleasing to Him, is answered in that, whoever he may be, so long as there does not follow from assisting him in that beloved matter something hated by Allah that is greater than it. This is among the most subtle, difficult, and burdensome matters for the souls. For this reason some of the Companions found it constricting, and 'Umar said what he said, until he did deeds after it. As for al-Siddiq, he received it with contentment and submission, until his heart was upon the heart of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) concerning it. And he answered 'Umar about what he asked regarding it with the very answer of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). This indicates that al-Siddiq, may Allah be pleased with him, is the best of the Companions, the most complete, the most knowing of Allah and His Messenger (ﷺ), the most knowledgeable of his religion, the most upright in pursuing what Allah loves, and the most in agreement with him. For this reason, 'Umar asked about what had occurred to him only the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and his close friend (al-Siddiq), to the exclusion of the rest of his Companions.

Among its lessons: the Prophet (ﷺ) turned to the right toward al-Hudaybiyyah. Al-Shafi'i said: part of it is from the lawful area (*al-hill*) and part of it is from the sacred area (*al-haram*).

Imam Ahmad narrated in this story that the Prophet (ﷺ) "used to pray in the sacred area while he was in the lawful area." In this there is something like an indication that the multiplied reward of prayer in Makkah pertains to the entire sacred area, not only the mosque where the circumambulation takes place. And that his saying: "A prayer in al-Masjid al-Haram is better than a hundred prayers in my mosque" is like His saying, the Exalted: ﴿So let them not approach al-Masjid al-Haram﴾ [al-Tawbah: 28], and His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Glory be to the One who took His servant by night from al-Masjid al-Haram﴾, and the Night Journey began from the house of Umm Hani'.

Among its lessons: whoever descends near Makkah should descend in the lawful area and pray in the sacred area. Ibn 'Umar used to do exactly this.

Among its lessons: it is permissible for the leader to initiate seeking peace with the enemy when he sees a benefit for the Muslims in it, and this does not depend on the initiative of the request coming from them.

In the standing of al-Mughirah ibn Shu'bah over the head of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) with a sword, and it was not his custom to have someone stand over his head while he was seated, there is a Sunnah to be followed when the envoys of the enemy arrive, in displaying honor and pride, glorifying the leader and obeying him, and protecting him with lives. This is the custom that prevails when the envoys of the believers come to the disbelievers, and when the envoys of the disbelievers come to the believers. This is not of the kind that the Prophet (ﷺ) censured with his saying: "Whoever loves that men should stand for him, let him take his seat in the Fire." Just as pride and vainglory in war are not of the blameworthy kind found elsewhere. And in sending the camels in the face of the other envoy there is evidence for the recommendation of displaying the symbols of Islam to the envoys of the disbelievers.

In the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ) to al-Mughirah: "As for Islam, I accept it; as for the wealth, I have nothing to do with it," there is evidence that the property of a polytheist under treaty is protected, and that it is not owned, but must be returned to him. For al-Mughirah had accompanied them under safe conduct, then betrayed them and took their wealth. The Prophet (ﷺ) did not address their property, nor defended it, nor guaranteed it for them, because that was before al-Mughirah's conversion to Islam.

In the saying of al-Siddiq to 'Urwah: "Suck the clitoris of al-Lat!" there is evidence for the permissibility of explicitly naming the private part when there is an interest that the situation requires, just as the Prophet (ﷺ) permitted that one who made a claim of the Jahiliyyah be addressed explicitly with the penis of his father, and be told: "Bite the penis of your father," and he was not spoken to with euphemism. For every station there is a fitting speech.
